Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test failure and bug report indicate that when calling appendFixedWidthPadRight with a null argument, a NullPointerException occurs if the null text representation has not been explicitly set. Examining the method StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar), the code checks if obj is null and if so, tries to use getNullText() to obtain the string to append. The critical code snippet is:

```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
int strLen = str.length();
```

The getNullText() method simply returns the field nullText, which in the default constructor of StrBuilder is not assigned any value (at least not shown in the snippets), so it is likely null by default. Therefore, when obj is null and getNullText() returns null, str is assigned null, and calling str.length() causes a NullPointerException.

This explains the failing test case where appendFixedWidthPadRight(null, 10, '*') is called on a newly created StrBuilder (which didn't set null text), resulting in a null pointer exception.

The provided recent bug reports don't contribute additional insight for this problem.

Hence, the underlying bug is that appendFixedWidthPadRight does not handle the case when getNullText() returns null. It should provide a default string (e.g., empty string or "null") when nullText is not explicitly set.

This diagnosis aligns perfectly with the current bug report summary: "StrBuilder appendFixedWidth does not handle nulls" and the description about NullPointerException when getNullText() is unset.

# Next step: The method to fix is StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object, int, char), likely by adding a null check or default value for the nullText. Also potentially, the constructor or nullText field initialization could be enhanced for safety.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
